proposals.evidence: The full compound is cut/bite + gave, with the auxiliary’s diy-/dīd- past stem. Turner 6140 branch 3 explicitly distinguishes this past formation, including Hindi diyā and Gujarati dīdhũ; Platts records kāṭ-denā as an intensive. The intervocalic/retroflex spelling variation is retained.
